title.narrative: Eighth Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme (Tranche II)

description.narrative: 1. The main outcome from SGP interventions is twofold: generate global environmental benefits and enhance local livelihoods within a framework of socio-ecological resilience. The programme will provide financial grants and technical assistance to civil society organization to implement community-led solutions. 2. Small scale farmers, livestock producers, fishermen and other smallholders will be supported to use improved agro-ecological practices and nature-based solutions and ecosystem-based approaches to enable sustainable agri-food systems across mosaics of natural and productive landscapes and seascapes in line with relevant national strategies and plans. Local communities in both rural and urban areas will be enabled to use sustainable urban solutions, access cost-effective renewable and clean energy solutions including in urban setups and remote rural sites and outer islands, explore alternatives to the use of harmful chemicals including through integrated pest management and biofertilizers, and champion efficient solutions for sustainable waste management. Financial grants, technical assistance and capacity building provided to SGP grantees and implementing partners will benefit an estimated 45,000 direct beneficiaries, including 22,500 women, 7,200 youth and 7,200 people with disabilities. 3. Based on the above, SGP interventions are expected to: create local jobs (through training and labor required to implement community-led initiatives), support rural residents diversify their income and strengthen livelihoods (income generating initiatives including ecotourism, beekeeping, and agroforestry), while building capacities and skills, empowering local communities and strengthening resilience.4. The specific focus on women, youth, IPLCS, people with disability will ensure that marginalized and under-represented social groups are empowered to benefit from SGP interventions. The Environmental and Social Management Framework developed will enable the SGP country teams to track relevant decent work standards such as safe working conditions and fair wages in line with the applicable regulations.

Community-based and civil society organizations are technically and financially supported to design and deliver locally led initiatives that address complex socio-ecological challenges to foster resilience, enhance livelihoods and deliver global environmental benefits.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
